main_result.title: In a rare process-level mismatch regime, a simple fixed bounded-mgf average-mean mixture can materially outperform the 2025 Chugg-Ramdas empirical-Bernstein CS on zero and many sparse-mismatch paths, while the empirical-Bernstein method can still be slightly tighter on some early-mismatch paths.

external_method.paper: Ben Chugg and Aaditya Ramdas, Closed-form empirical Bernstein confidence sequences for scalars and matrices, arXiv:2512.21300v1, 2025-12-24
external_method.paper_claim_scope: variance-adaptive CS for the average conditional mean of bounded variables; no stationarity assumption; paper reports strong generic width performance up to about 1e6 samples
external_method.implementation_used_for_worker_local_ben: CR_mixture_exact with public compute_Ut / find_y_star_stable formulas; kappa=.25 (paper figure default) and kappa=4 (a predeclared alternative close to the observed zero-path plateau).

zero_mismatch_alpha_0_05.interpretation: For an all-zero rare-mismatch stream, the public variance-adaptive CR mixture spends substantial width on a generic empirical-Bernstein geometry. The one-sided bounded-chord mixture directly targets the upper rare-rate tail and reaches 1% with about 35% fewer clusters than CR at its observed large-kappa plateau and about 64% fewer than the paper's kappa=.25 default. This is a low-rate task-specific comparison, not a generic statement that CR is worse.

broader_worker_local_grid.grid: n in {200,400,800,1600}; mismatch count in {0,1,2,5,10}; placement in {early, late, spread}; duplicate placements removed for zero-mismatch => 52 distinct scenarios
broader_worker_local_grid.interpretation: At kappa=4 the empirical-Bernstein CS can be up to about 1.8% tighter in this grid, chiefly when sparse mismatches arrive early and help its predictable variance estimate. Late mismatches are much more costly for CR because its width depends on path/order; the fixed bounded mixture depends only on cumulative score and is order-invariant.

main_result.important_time_varying_estimand_guard: Do not apply a running intersection across time to tighten intervals when the target is the time-varying average conditional mean: the estimand itself changes with t. A running intersection is appropriate only under a constant-parameter contract or a separately proved envelope target.

adaptive_dependence_sanity_not_proof.simulation: 30,000 trajectories, 500 clusters, Bernoulli conditional means chosen from past outcomes; evaluated ever-crossing at the true pathwise running average conditional mean.

patterns.conditional_p: .005 when observed running mismatch rate >1%, else .04

adaptive_dependence_sanity_not_proof.scope: These implementation stresses are not a proof; the supermartingale domination is the validity argument.

measurement_validity_rules: Benchmark confidence sequences on the actual deployment decision region. Generic average interval width can hide large inefficiency in one-sided rare-failure certification.

When the target is time-varying average conditional mean, path/order dependence of a variance-adaptive CS is legitimate, but running-intersection tightening across different t changes the estimand and must not be used without a separate theorem.

A method parameter such as kappa must be chosen before the current outcome or via a valid mixture; reporting the best kappa separately per realized path would be post-selection and is not a valid certificate.
A simpler bound that dominates on zero/rare paths may still lose on higher-variance or early-failure paths; do not generalize this low-rate benchmark to generic bounded-mean estimation.
scope_guards: The Chugg-Ramdas benchmark was reconstructed from the authors' public methods.py and utils.py in worker-local Python; no modification to their repository was made.
The tested CR implementation is the exact mixture implementation, not the closed-form approximation, and the default/tuned kappa comparisons are explicitly separated.
The broad grid is synthetic binary cluster-score data, not measured production mismatch traffic.
No forbidden semantic inputs were read.

frontier.action: Optimize the fixed lambda/weight mixture ex ante for a declared rare-mismatch design envelope and compare worst-case sparse-failure delay to CR_kappa=4 without using realized outcomes to select the winner.
Build a lifetime-valid fingerprint generation/lease protocol that defaults to average-mean inference and permits stable-p inference only under an independently justified constant-mean contract.
Benchmark fractional cluster scores and unequal cluster sizes, separating equal-process reliability from request-weighted reliability rather than silently changing the estimand.
Continue public trace search for token-to-score/sign propagation.

exact_next_action: Optimize a predeclared lambda/weight portfolio for the 0.1%-5% rare-mismatch region under zero plus sparse-failure scenarios, with a robustness constraint against early/late mismatch placement.
